output.statement: Let a,b be distinct nonzero integers with ab+1 a rational square, and let x=u/v be a rational number in lowest terms, v>0, such that ax+1 and bx+1 are rational squares (zero squares are allowed). For an odd prime p, write e=v_p(v), alpha=v_p(a), beta=v_p(b), a_0=a/p^alpha, and b_0=b/p^beta. If e>max(alpha,beta), then the residue of a_0/b_0 modulo p is a nonzero quadratic residue. Consequently, if this residue is a nonresidue, every such common neighbor satisfies v_p(v)<=max(alpha,beta).
assumptions: a,b are distinct nonzero integers and ab+1 is a rational square.
x=u/v is rational in lowest terms with v>0.
ax+1 and bx+1 are rational squares; their square roots may be zero.
quantifiers: For every pair a,b satisfying the assumptions.
For every rational x=u/v satisfying the assumptions.
For every odd prime p, if v_p(v)>max(v_p(a),v_p(b)), then the stated residue is a nonzero quadratic residue.
output.proof:
Put d_a=gcd(|a|,v) and d_b=gcd(|b|,v). Since gcd(u,v)=1, gcd(au+v,v)=d_a and gcd(bu+v,v)=d_b. Reducing ax+1 and bx+1 to lowest terms, their denominators are v/d_a and v/d_b. A reduced rational square has square numerator and denominator, including when its numerator is zero. Hence there are positive integers r,s and nonnegative integers A,B such that

v=d_a r^2=d_b s^2,   au+v=d_a A^2,   bu+v=d_b B^2.

Suppose e>max(alpha,beta). Then p divides v, so p does not divide u, and v_p(d_a)=alpha, v_p(d_b)=beta. Define d_{a,0}=d_a/p^alpha and d_{b,0}=d_b/p^beta; these and a_0,b_0 are p-adic units. Divide the first numerator equation by p^alpha and reduce modulo p. Since e>alpha, p divides v/p^alpha, giving a_0u ≡ d_{a,0}A^2 (mod p). The second equation likewise gives b_0u ≡ d_{b,0}B^2 (mod p). Their left sides are nonzero modulo p; thus A and B are nonzero modulo p. Dividing the congruences yields

A^2/B^2 ≡ (a_0/b_0)(d_{b,0}/d_{a,0}) (mod p).

The denominator equations give d_b/d_a=r^2/s^2, a rational square. Its p-adic valuation beta-alpha is even, and after removing that p-power its unit part d_{b,0}/d_{a,0} is a square modulo p: indeed, write r/s=p^k q with q a p-adic unit, so d_b/d_a=p^{2k}q^2 and d_{b,0}/d_{a,0}≡q^2 modulo p. Therefore the displayed congruence implies that a_0/b_0 is a square modulo p. The conclusion is nonzero because a_0 and b_0 are units. In particular, when that residue is a nonresidue, the strict inequality assumed for e is impossible.

The denominator equations also imply the exact parity conditions e-min(e,alpha) even and e-min(e,beta) even. If e is at most both alpha and beta, they impose no restriction; if e exceeds both, they require alpha and beta to have the same parity and e to share that parity; if alpha<e<=beta, they require e-alpha even, with the symmetric condition when beta<e<=alpha. The residue conclusion above is an additional necessary condition in the strict deep-denominator case, obtained from the simultaneous numerator squares. Zero numerator roots cause no exception: in that case the reduced congruence in this strict case would force the corresponding root to be nonzero modulo p.

extracted_claim_proposals.statement: At any odd prime p for which the p-free parts of two distinct nonzero integer anchors have a nonresidue ratio, no rational common neighbor can have a reduced denominator whose p-adic valuation exceeds both anchor valuations.
assumptions: a,b are distinct nonzero integers with ab+1 a rational square.
x=u/v is a common rational neighbor in lowest terms with v>0.
p is odd and the residue of (a/p^v_p(a))/(b/p^v(b)) modulo p is a nonresidue.
quantifiers: For every such a,b,x and p.

output.method_summary: Scope: this is a fully proved local restriction on common-neighbor denominators, not a resolution of the sextuple problem. The reduced numerator-square equations are used along with denominator squares: when the denominator valuation is strictly greater than both anchor valuations, reducing both numerator equations modulo p and taking their ratio forces a quadratic-residue condition on the anchor p-free parts. This gives an additional obstruction at primes where that ratio is a nonresidue; it does not constrain every anchor pair or every prime. The all-positive sextuple case and the unrestricted-sign case both remain unresolved in the supplied evidence: there is no exact witness or unbounded-height obstruction. Opposite-sign integer anchors in a tuple must be {-1,1}; negating all elements handles same-sign anchors, without forcing the other elements positive.

direction_proposals.label: Combine local residues with cross-neighbor equations
direction_proposals.assignment: For fixed distinct integer anchors a,b with ab+1 a rational square, combine the proved deep-denominator residue restriction with the simultaneous parametrization of common neighbors and all six cross-pair square conditions. Seek an all-height obstruction to four distinct nonzero pairwise adjacent common neighbors, or identify a precise obstruction to this route. Preserve zero square roots and exclude zero or repeated elements.

target_claim.statement: For every pair of distinct nonzero integer anchors a,b with ab+1 a rational square, there do not exist four distinct nonzero rational common neighbors that are pairwise adjacent under the condition xy+1 is a rational square.
quantifiers: Universally over all such anchor pairs and all rational common neighbors, with no height bound.
